reason: E1 shows that Mo-containing RMPEAs (e.g., MoNbTaW, MoNbTaVW) retain yield strength better at high temperature than Al- or Hf-containing alloys, supporting the general benefit of Mo. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides direct evidence that adding Mo to TiVNbTa maintains a single-phase BCC structure, enhances strength by 30–50% at 1273 K, or preserves ductility above 30% strain; these specific claims are extrapolations without cited support.
premises: Mo-containing refractory HEAs retain yield strength better at high temperature than Al- or Hf-containing ones
MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW show weak temperature dependence of yield strength up to 1600 °C
Adding Mo to TiVNbTa will maintain a single-phase BCC structure
Mo addition increases lattice distortion and solid solution strengthening at high temperature
The predicted 30–50% yield strength gain at 1273 K is achievable without unacceptable ductility loss
